## Step 1 — `ZimmSlideIndicator` molecule

Create ONLY these 4 files:
```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/index.tsx
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/index.stories.tsx
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/index.test.tsx
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts
```
Plus register it in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (add one import + one entry to the existing `components` export object — do not touch any other line in that file).

**Do not touch any other file. Do not create any other component from the plan (that's later steps).**

## Design source
Figma `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`, node `40002536:7957` "Slide indicator" — a 1px-tall hairline strip (verified: 159.11×1 / 99.44×1 depending on `Qty images`), flush to the image's bottom edge. NOT floating dots — do not assume dot geometry; render it as a segmented hairline/bar strip matching that 1px height, one segment per image, the active segment visually distinguished (e.g. differing opacity/width via the recipe). 13 Figma variants total: `Qty images` = 5 | 8, `Slide selected` = 1..N.

## CRITICAL — this is NOT a duplicate-with-arrows situation, it is touch-ONLY
Per the plan's §4a (Marcel's resolved decision): "position indicator is just for tablet and mobile, desktop hover is arrows." This component is the read-only position indicator that appears ONLY where hover is unavailable (touch devices). It has NO buttons, NO click handlers — it is purely a visual + accessible readout of "which image am I on". The arrows (a separate component, built in a later step) are what desktop uses instead.

## Reference pattern to copy exactly
Read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx` and its sibling `.css.ts`, `.stories.tsx`, `.test.tsx` FIRST, in full, before writing anything. Copy its conventions precisely:
- Named export (PascalCase, e.g. `export const ZimmSlideIndicator = (...) => {...}`) AND a default export (`export default ZimmSlideIndicator`) — this component has no lazy-load consumer yet but match the existing dual-export convention used across ui-kits atoms/molecules for consistency.
- Props type declared inline at top of file, named `ZimmSlideIndicatorProps`, NOT exported (no sibling needs it — this component's props are primitive: `count: number`, `activeIndex: number`).
- Recipe key as a module-level string const: `const ZIMM_SLIDE_INDICATOR_RECIPE = 'ZimmSlideIndicator'`.
- `useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_SLIDE_INDICATOR_RECIPE, {isActive})` — actually the props object passed should be whatever the per-segment styling needs; study exactly how zimmColourSwatchGroup passes its props object to the recipe and match that shape (it may be at the root call, with `isActive` applied per rendered element — read the exemplar closely, don't guess).
- Apply parts via `<chakra.div __css={styles.partName}>` — `__css`, not `sx`, `chakra.*` primitives not `Box`/`Flex`.
- All colour/spacing values in the `.css.ts` file as `var(--zimm-*)` custom properties. NEVER a bare Chakra token key (e.g. `gap: 'xs'` is FORBIDDEN — must be `gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'`). This is mechanically enforced by `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` — your test run will fail if you get this wrong.
- Responsive values (if any) as explicit `[`@media (min-width: ${BP.x})`]` blocks — never Chakra's array shorthand `['a','b','c']`, which the same guard test fails on every element.

## Recipe file (`zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts`)
```ts
export const ZimmSlideIndicator = {
  parts: ['root', 'dot'],
  baseStyle: (props: {isActive?: boolean}): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({ ... }),
};
```
No default export. The recipe key name `ZimmSlideIndicator` must NOT collide with any base SFCC recipe name — it doesn't, this is a net-new name, so you're safe, but confirm by checking `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/theme/components/` has no `slide-indicator.js` or similar (there is a guard test in `recipeGuards.test.ts` for this — read it to understand what it checks).

## Registration
In `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`, add:
```ts
import {ZimmSlideIndicator} from '../../components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/zimmSlideIndicator.css'
```
(match the exact relative-path style already used for the other ui-kits imports in that file — read the file first to copy the exact import path convention), and add `ZimmSlideIndicator,` to the `components` export object, matching alphabetical/grouping convention already present.

## Component behaviour and exact pass criteria (all must be true)
- Props: `count: number`, `activeIndex: number`.
- Renders exactly `count` segment/dot nodes as children of the `root` part.
- Exactly one node carries the "active" treatment, for any `activeIndex` value that is `>= 0` and `< count`.
- **Out-of-range `activeIndex` clamps rather than throwing** — if `activeIndex < 0`, treat as `0`; if `activeIndex >= count`, treat as `count - 1`. Write this clamping explicitly, do not rely on `Array.map` silently doing nothing sensible.
- **`count <= 1` renders nothing** — return `null` (or render the root with zero children — but the test should assert nothing meaningful is on screen; prefer returning `null` from the component entirely for `count <= 0`, and also for `count === 1` since a single image has nothing to indicate position among).
- **The root is EXPOSED and ANNOUNCED to assistive tech — it must NOT be `aria-hidden`.** This is a corrected requirement (see §4a of the plan): because this indicator is the ONLY position signal on touch devices (no arrows exist there to announce it instead), hiding it would be a WCAG 1.1.1 information-loss violation. Implement an accessible announcement of position — e.g. a visually-hidden text node inside the root reading something like "Image {activeIndex + 1} of {count}" (use `defineMessages` + `useIntl` with a parameterized message, matching the i18n convention in `zimmColourSwatchGroup`), OR `role="group"` with a computed `aria-label` of the same shape. Pick whichever matches the exemplar's i18n conventions most closely. Do NOT ship it aria-hidden — a test will explicitly assert this.
- `parts` array in the recipe must EXACTLY equal the set of `styles.X` reads in `index.tsx` — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` enforces this by walking your file; if you read `styles.root` and `styles.dot`, your `parts` array must be exactly `['root', 'dot']`, no more, no less.
- Component appears correctly in the `components` export in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.

## Story (`index.stories.tsx`)
- `title: 'Elements/ZimmSlideIndicator'` (per `.claude/rules/components.md` categorisation — this is a generic building block, not commerce-specific by itself).
- Mandatory `Default` export.
- Named exports for meaningful states: e.g. `FiveImages` (count=5), `EightImages` (count=8), `LastSelected` (activeIndex = count-1), `FirstSelected` (activeIndex=0).
- No `play` function needed — this is a purely visual/display component with no interaction to assert (it has no click handlers).

## Test (`index.test.tsx`)
Vitest + React Testing Library. Cover, at minimum:
- Renders exactly `count` segment nodes for count=5 and count=8.
- Exactly one active segment for activeIndex at first (0), middle, and last (count-1) positions.
- `activeIndex = -1` clamps to treating index 0 as active (does not throw).
- `activeIndex = count` (i.e. one past the end) clamps to treating the last index active (does not throw).
- `count = 0` renders null / nothing.
- `count = 1` renders null / nothing.
- The root is NOT `aria-hidden="true"` — assert this explicitly (query for the root and assert `aria-hidden` attribute is absent or `false`).
- Some accessible text/label exists reflecting position (assert on whatever your accessible-announcement mechanism produces — a get-by-text match on the visually-hidden text, or an aria-label match).
- Mock `useMultiStyleConfig` to return a flat parts object (`{root: {}, dot: {}}`) so no real Chakra theme is needed — copy this mock pattern exactly from `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.test.tsx`.
- Wrap renders in `IntlProvider` if you used `defineMessages`/`useIntl` (required — `useIntl` throws without a provider). Copy the render-helper pattern from the exemplar test file.

## House rules (apply to every file you write)
- TypeScript only (`.tsx`/`.ts`), no `.js`/`.jsx`.
- No `any` without a comment explaining why. No non-null assertion (`!`) without a comment.
- Australian spelling in any new identifiers/comments you author (not relevant here, no colour-adjacent naming in this component, but keep in mind for later steps).
- No hardcoded hex/px/rem/em literal anywhere in `index.tsx` or the recipe — everything through `var(--zimm-*)`.
- Do NOT add a `console.log` anywhere.
- Do not modify `package.json` — no new dependencies.

## When done
Report back: the exact list of files created/modified with line counts, and confirm you did NOT touch any file outside this list. Do NOT stage or commit anything — that happens later in the loop, after testing and scoring.

2	import { SWATCHES_PER_PAGE } from './zimmColourSwatchGroupShared';
3	
4	/**
5	 * Recipe for the PDP colour-swatch group — the "Colour: Bay Blue" label row, and (when there is
6	 * more than one populated colour) the row of ZimmColourSwatch rectangles beneath it. This recipe
7	 * only lays the group out; each swatch's own fill/border/focus styling stays in the sibling
8	 * ZimmColourSwatch atom's own recipe.
9	 *
10	 * Values below are read directly off Figma for this exact component, not estimated — node
11	 * 40000307:13867 ("ColourOptions"), within Zimmermann_Design_System_2026.
12	 *
13	 * Six parts:
14	 *   - `root` — outer vertical flex container: the label row above, the swatches row below.
15	 *     Capped to a fixed `maxWidth` (`GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH`, see below) unconditionally — not just
16	 *     when paginated — so `labelName`'s truncation CSS always has a definite width to truncate
17	 *     against. See this part's own baseStyle comment for the full explanation.
18	 *   - `label` — the label row ("labelContainer" in Figma): the label-group (the two
19	 *     "Colour:"/name text pieces — laid out via a plain Chakra-prop wrapper in the component
20	 *     itself, not a seventh part here; see index.tsx's own comment for why) plus the pagination
21	 *     controls, right-aligned purely via the label-group's own `flex: 1 0 0` rather than an
22	 *     absolute-position hack.
23	 *   - `labelName` — the dynamic colour-name text specifically (e.g. "Bay Blue"). Gets its own
24	 *     part, unlike the static "Colour:" piece beside it, because it alone carries the
25	 *     Figma-mandated truncation behaviour: "If Label/Colour name is longer, use truncation"
26	 *     (this node's own interaction annotation).
27	 *   - `swatches` — the horizontal row of rendered ZimmColourSwatch children. Once paginated
28	 *     (`isPaginated`), reserves a fixed page-width footprint regardless of how many items the
29	 *     current window actually renders — see its own baseStyle comment below for the layout bug
30	 *     this prevents.
31	 *   - `pagination` — wrapper around the two chevron buttons.
32	 *   - `pageButton` — each individual chevron button (24x24, holding a 16px ZimmIcon).
33	 */
34	
35	/**
36	 * Imported from the shared zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts module — the same shared-module
37	 * precedent theme/components/footerShared.ts already sets — rather than retyped here, so
38	 * index.tsx, this recipe, and the test file can never disagree with each other. Aliased to the
39	 * shorter `PAGE_SIZE` name since this file's only use is the `GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH` calc
40	 * expression below.
41	 */
42	const PAGE_SIZE = SWATCHES_PER_PAGE;
43	
44	/**
45	 * The reserved 4-swatch-wide footprint: PAGE_SIZE swatches at the atom's own fixed 47px width
46	 * (see `swatch.width` in zimmColourSwatch.css.ts), with no per-swatch gap
47	 * (`swatches.gap` below is 0, same as the atom's own adjacency). Two consumers share this one
48	 * value rather than each typing their own copy of the same `calc(...)` expression:
49	 *   - `swatches.width`/`minWidth`, applied only once paginated (see that part below) — keeps the
50	 *     footprint constant across a full page vs. a shorter final page.
51	 *   - `root.maxWidth`, applied unconditionally regardless of pagination (see that part below) —
52	 *     caps the whole component so `labelName`'s truncation CSS always has a definite width to
53	 *     truncate against.
54	 */
55	const GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH = `calc(${PAGE_SIZE} * var(--zimm-scale-1200))`;
56	
57	export const ZimmColourSwatchGroup = {
58	  parts: ['root', 'label', 'labelName', 'swatches', 'pagination', 'pageButton'],
59	
60	  baseStyle: ({ isPaginated }: { isPaginated?: boolean }): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
61	    root: {
62	      display: 'flex',
63	      flexDirection: 'column',
64	      // 8px between the label row and the swatches row. No background here — background lives
65	      // per-swatch, already handled by the atom's own recipe.
66	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
67	      // Unconditional cap, regardless of `isPaginated` — this is a bug fix, not a stylistic
68	      // choice. `root` otherwise has no width of its own (deliberate — see the `swatches` part
69	      // below for why a short, non-paginated row must still size naturally to its actual content)
70	      // so it has no ceiling for `labelName`'s truncation CSS to truncate against: confirmed via
71	      // real Chromium rendering that a long enough colour name simply grows `root` (and the
72	      // flex-grown `labelName` span inside it) past this footprint with no ellipsis, unless some
73	      // ancestor happens to impose a definite width of its own. Capping `root` itself to the same
74	      // reserved footprint `swatches` already reserves once paginated makes truncation
75	      // self-contained in every context, rather than depending on whatever the eventual PDP page
76	      // does or doesn't constrain. `maxWidth`, not `width`: `root` must still be free to render
77	      // narrower than this when content is short (e.g. one or two short colour names) — this only
78	      // ever stops it from growing past the cap. Does not change the swatches row's own sizing
79	      // behaviour (still `100%` when non-paginated, see below) — it only changes what that `100%`
80	      // now resolves against.
81	      maxWidth: GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH,
82	    },
83	
84	    label: {
85	      display: 'flex',
86	      alignItems: 'center',
87	      // 24px. Matches spacing.xl exactly, so the named step is used rather than the numerically
88	      // identical --zimm-scale-600 alias — see bottomBar.css.ts's own `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`
89	      // usage for the same 24px value elsewhere in this codebase.
90	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',
91	      // 8px between the label-group and the pagination controls.
92	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
93	    },
94	
95	    labelName: {
96	      textStyle: 'caption',
97	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
98	      // The truncating half of the label-group's two text pieces (the static "Colour:" text
99	      // beside it never truncates — see index.tsx). `flex: 1 0 0` lets it consume the
100	      // label-group's remaining width; `minWidth: 0` is required for a flex item to actually
101	      // shrink below its content size instead of overflowing; the rest is the standard
102	      // single-line-ellipsis triad.
103	      flex: '1 0 0',
104	      minWidth: 0,
105	      overflow: 'hidden',
106	      textOverflow: 'ellipsis',
107	      whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
108	    },
109	
110	    swatches: {
111	      display: 'flex',
112	      // Required so that off-page swatches (position:absolute, see index.tsx) are contained
113	      // within this element rather than escaping to the nearest positioned ancestor.
114	      position: 'relative',
115	      // Non-paginated (<= SWATCHES_PER_PAGE populated colours): sizes naturally to however many
116	      // swatches are actually present. Unchanged, deliberately out of scope for this fix — there
117	      // is no confirmed design value either way for a 2- or 3-colour row's width, so nothing was
118	      // invented here.
119	      //
120	      // Paginated (> SWATCHES_PER_PAGE populated colours, windowed to a fixed PAGE_SIZE-wide
121	      // slice per page): a plain `100%` here resolves against `root`'s own width — but `root` has
122	      // no explicit width of its own, so it auto-fits to its widest child, which is this very
123	      // element. That circular relationship meant the *rendered* width tracked how many items the
124	      // current window actually held (192px for a full 4-item page, 96px for a 2-item final
125	      // page), so `root` — and `label` above it, itself 100% of that same `root` — visibly
126	      // resized between pages. Confirmed directly in a running Storybook: the pagination chevrons
127	      // jumped position between the two pages of the `Paginated` story. Reserving
128	      // GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH regardless of the current page's real item count breaks that
129	      // loop — the footprint stays constant across every page, full or partial. A partial final
130	      // page's unused space simply remains empty to the right: the flex default
131	      // `justify-content: flex-start` already left-aligns the rendered items, so nothing further
132	      // is needed for that.
133	      width: isPaginated ? GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH : '100%',
134	      ...(isPaginated ? { minWidth: GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH } : {}),
135	      // Confirmed directly off the Figma export, not a stylistic default: the 4-swatch example
136	      // measures exactly 192px total width for four 48px-wide swatches (4 x 48, no gap
137	      // contribution) — swatches sit directly adjacent. Do not add a gap here; that would be a
138	      // real deviation from the design, not a stylistic default.
139	      gap: 0,
140	    },
141	
142	    pagination: {
143	      display: 'flex',
144	      alignItems: 'center',
145	      // No inter-button gap value exists in the Figma export handed to this step — left at the
146	      // flex default (no `gap` declared at all) rather than invented. Revisit if a designer
147	      // confirms a real value.
148	    },
149	
150	    pageButton: {
151	      display: 'flex',
152	      alignItems: 'center',
153	      justifyContent: 'center',
154	      width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px
155	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px
156	      // Resets the native <button> UA chrome so the box is exactly the 24x24 the design calls
157	      // for, with the 16px ZimmIcon centred inside it by the flex alignment above.
158	      padding: 0,
159	      border: 'none',
160	      background: 'none',
161	      cursor: 'pointer',
162	      // No confirmed Figma spec for a disabled visual treatment on this control — same "leave an
163	      // unspecified visual state alone rather than invent one" precedent as swatch-group's own
164	      // disabled colour logic (see this codebase's Known Gaps notes). The native `disabled`
165	      // attribute (set in index.tsx) already makes the control genuinely inert and announces as
166	      // disabled to assistive tech; only the cursor affordance is set here, which is a UX
167	      // keyword, not a design token.
168	      _disabled: {
169	        cursor: 'not-allowed',
170	        color: 'var(--zimm-color-icon-disabled)',
171	      },
172	      // Same uniform ring every other interactive control in ui-kits/ uses (zimmColourSwatch,
173	      // zimmNavItem) — --zimm-focus-ring already composites the border-width/colour pair.
174	      _focusVisible: {
175	        outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
176	        outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
177	      },
178	    },
179	  }),

140	## 4a. Arrows vs. indicator — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)
141	
142	> *"position indicator is just for tablet and mobile, desktop hover is arrows"*
143	
144	The two are **mutually exclusive**, not paired. Consequences for Steps 1 and 4:
145	
146	**Split by pointer capability, not viewport width.** The gate is
147	`@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` — the same gate every other hover rule already uses:
148	
149	- **hover-capable + fine pointer** → prev/next arrow buttons, revealed on `:hover, :focus-within`. No indicator.
150	- **everything else (touch tablet, mobile)** → `ZimmSlideIndicator`, always visible. No arrows.
151	
152	Capability rather than width is what actually delivers the stated intent: the 768 artboard is a *touch* tablet,
153	and a width rule alone would give it arrows it can never hover to reveal. It also keeps this consistent with the
154	card's own hover rules rather than introducing a second, differently-keyed breakpoint. **Edge case, accepted:**
155	a desktop browser resized below 768 keeps arrows (it still has a fine pointer); a touch-screen laptop gets the
156	indicator. Both are the safe failure direction — nobody is shown a control they cannot operate.

159	
160	1. **Step 1 — the indicator is NOT `aria-hidden` on touch.** The original criterion assumed the arrow buttons
161	   announce position, so the indicator could be hidden as duplicate. Where the indicator renders there are **no
162	   arrows**, so it becomes the only position signal — hiding it would be a 1.1.1 information loss. It needs an
163	   accessible position announcement (e.g. a visually-hidden "Image 3 of 8" live region, or `role="group"` with
164	   `aria-label`). Revised criterion: exposed and announced when it is the sole affordance.

170	## 4b. Touch image paging — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)
171	
172	> *"scroll-snap it is"*
173	
174	Native CSS scroll-snap. The dots remain a **passive readout**, visually unchanged from Figma — no enlargement,
175	no conversion to tap targets, so no departure from the design and no WCAG 2.5.8 problem to solve.
176	
177	**Implementation shape: one scroll container on every breakpoint, not two mechanisms.**
178	
179	The image strip is always a horizontally scrollable flex container with `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` and
180	`scrollSnapAlign: 'start'` on each slide. What differs by pointer capability is only the *affordance* layered
181	over it:
182	
183	| | Mechanism | Affordance |
184	|---|---|---|
185	| hover + fine pointer | same scroll container | arrows call `scrollBy()`; no indicator |
186	| touch | same scroll container | native drag; indicator reflects position |
187	
188	One container rather than two code paths means a single source of truth for "which image is showing", the
189	arrows become progressive enhancement over something that already works, and the desktop path inherits
190	keyboard scrollability for free.
191	
192	**Active-index derivation:** prefer `IntersectionObserver` on the slides over a scroll listener — 60 tiles on a
193	PLP make a per-scroll-event listener a real perf cost, and the repo already has
194	`overrides/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer.ts` (**Tier 2 — import it, do not modify it**). The `scrollend`
195	event is an acceptable alternative. Left to the Implementer; either satisfies the pass criteria.
196	
197	**Precedent:** the base `ProductScroller`
198	(`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-scroller/index.jsx:79-84`) already uses
199	`scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` with `overflowX: 'scroll'`. Same technique, already proven in this codebase.
200	
201	**Accepted caveat:** swipe has no explicit affordance beyond the dots implying further content. This is the
202	universal mobile convention, and the alternative (enlarging 1px dots into 24×24 tap targets) trades an
203	invisible-but-expected gesture for a visible-but-off-design control. **Action: flag to Kiera that the mobile
204	gesture is undocumented in the design**, so it lands in the spec rather than being discovered in QA.
205

207	- The slide container carries `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'`; every slide carries `scrollSnapAlign`.

209	  two never coexist in the same DOM.
